Brown, A. (Energy Insights), Waldheim, L. (Waldheim Consulting), Ebadian, M., Saddler, J. (UBC), Nylund, N.-O. and Aakko-Saksa, P. (VTT); Bacovsky, D. (ed.) (2020). The Role of Renewable Transport Fuels in Decarbonizing Road Transport - Production Technologies and Costs. AMF Annex 58 / IEA Bioenergy Task 41 Project 10, November 2020.

BACKGROUND ONLY - no extraction. What it is and why no data: Review of renewable fuel production routes (ethanol, biodiesel, HVO, biomethane, gasification, pyrolysis, HTL, e-fuels), feedstocks, policy and engine compatibility. Its only technology-level numbers, Table 4 (p.85: capital, feedstock and operating cost and total, EUR/GJ, low/high, for cellulosic ethanol, 1.5-generation ethanol, methanol/methane from biomass and waste, FT liquids from biomass and waste, bio-oil co-processing and stand-alone, HVO, AD biomethane; 10% finance, 15 years, 8 000 h/yr, 200 MW output) and Table 5 (p.88: costs after reductions), are reprinted from IEA Bioenergy Advanced Biofuels - Potential for Cost Reduction (Brown et al. 2020), which the database already holds and has extracted as brown_2020_001. Loading them again would duplicate that source. What it does have: Tables 4 and 5 (reprints of brown_2020_001); TRL statements: fast pyrolysis bio-oil TRL 8 (Ensyn, BTG, Valmet/Fortum, 10 000-50 000 t/yr; p.30), HTL continuous pilots TRL 5 with 4 000-16 000 t/yr prototypes in construction (p.31), sugar-to-hydrocarbon fermentation TRL 5-8, Virent catalytic TRL 5, algae TRL 5; electrolysis hydrogen TRL 9, other e-fuel routes TRL 4-6 (Fig. 1). Fuel prices: US ethanol 13-15 EUR/GJ, biodiesel 19-24 EUR/GJ, fossil 8-14 EUR/GJ. Printed page = PDF page - 12.
